answer: Continuous work-history ledger. Every identity accumulates a public record of completed tasks, and rewards release only against that record. A clone starts with a hollow history, so it cannot claim high-value work until it has done low-value work for real. Attacker cost is the time and labor to build genuine history per clone, which scales linearly and cannot be copied or split. Records live in an append-only vault keyed to task outputs. Periodic mesa review audits a sample of records for consistency, flagging identities whose histories look manufactured.
